newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WOODS THE MAN TO BEAT AT AUGUSTA, MONTGOMERIE SAYS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS THE MAN TO BEAT AT AUGUSTA, MONTGOMERIE SAYS.

text.p: Golf sensation Tiger Woods will be the man to beat at April's U.S. Masters but he could falter on the Ryder Cup course at Sotogrande in Spain, European number one Colin Montgomerie said on Friday.
Montgomerie told a news conference Woods was the main obstacle between him and his first major title.
"My record in the U.S. Masters isn't as good as I'd like it to be but I can win there," he said. "I wouldn't be going if I didn't think I could. We've just got to get rid of Tiger Woods, that's all.
"It's incredible that someone of that age is capable of coping with all the pressure put upon him. I don't know if I could have done it when I was 21. He's obviously a very mature 21-year-old."

But Montgomerie said Woods, whose game is based on his awesome distance off the tee, will need tremendous mental as well as physical strength and technique if he is to emulate previous winners like Britain's Nick Faldo and Germany's Bernhard Langer.

Faldo won at Augusta in 1989 and 1990 after nail-biting play-offs and Langer triumphed in 1985 when he was still in his 20s. Langer won again in 1993 and Faldo claimed his third U.S. Masters last year.
"It takes the Faldo-Langer mental attitude to win that tournament as well as length, and everyone's talking about (Woods's) length, but we'll see how he goes," Montgomerie said.

He said Woods, who has won four titles since turning professional last August and powered his way to a 10-stroke victory in the Bangkok Classic last week, would find the Valderrama Ryder Cup course at Sotogrande trickier than Augusta.
"His greatest asset is his length and there are holes out there which don't accommodate for that. You can't afford to hit the ball too far, you can get yourself into trouble."
Montgomerie said he had fully recovered from a virus which he picked up in Asia last year but which was properly diagnosed only a fortnight ago while he was playing in Australia.

"I would never say I am ever in full health but I'm back to as good as I was," he said. "I'm watching what I eat for the first time ever. I'm fit enough to walk around 18 holes of a golf course and that's good enough to me."
